source_caption:
When Tom Hardy joined the cast to play the deeply eccentric, highly volatile London gang leader Alfie Solomons, he essentially threw the carefully polished scripts right out the window. Hardy famously improvised massive portions of his sprawling, fiercely intimidating monologues on the spot, deliberately changing his erratic delivery in every single take to keep his co-stars completely off balance. Cillian Murphy, playing the notoriously stoic Tommy Shelby, had to fight desperately just to stay in character while Hardy unleashed his utterly unhinged, heavily accented tangents. By bringing an atmosphere of absolute, chaotic unpredictability to the set, Hardy masterfully proves that the most magnetic on-screen villains are the ones who don’t even let the other actors know what they are going to do next.
⠀
Peaky Blinders (2013-2022), created by Steven Knight, starring Cillian Murphy, Paul Anderson, Sophie Rundle. In the fiercely violent, heavily industrialized aftermath of World War I, a brilliantly calculating, profoundly ambitious war veteran leads his family’s ruthless street gang on a wildly dangerous, deeply blood-soaked rise to massive political and criminal power in Birmingham, England.

source_details.title: Peaky Blinders
source_details.synopsis: Peaky Blinders is a British historical crime drama television series created by Steven Knight. Set in Birmingham, it follows the exploits of the Peaky Blinders crime gang in the direct aftermath of the First World War. The fictional gang is loosely based on an urban youth gang active in the city from the 1880s to the 1920s. The series features an ensemble cast: led by Cillian Murphy, starring as Tommy Shelby, Helen McCrory as Elizabeth "Polly" Gray, Paul Anderson as Arthur Shelby, Sophie Rundle as Ada Shelby, and Joe Cole as John Shelby, the group's senior members.
